definition: The conditioners of exertion named in the four bases of power: generating desire, making an effort, arousing energy, taking hold of the heart, and exerting oneself.
notes: Use exertion conditioner so the compound stays inside the governed saṅkhāra family alongside kāyasaṅkhāra, vacīsaṅkhāra, cittasaṅkhāra and āyusaṅkhāra, rather than drifting into volitional-formation language borrowed from the aggregate sense of saṅkhāra. Keep padhāna as exertion and sammā-vāyāma as effort: both verbs, vāyamati and padahati, appear in the same clause of the formula, so collapsing them makes one clause repeat another. SN 51.13 is the control passage: a base of power is defined there as a factor, the composure gained in dependence on it, and these conditioners together.

example_phrases.translation: these are called the exertion conditioners
example_phrases.notes: Closes each of the four rounds of the formula.

example_phrases.translation: the basis of power that possesses composure through desire together with the exertion conditioners
example_phrases.notes: Shows the compound inside the full definition of a base of power.

version_notes: Created from SN 51.13 and aligned with the governed conditioner family.

translation_policy.default_scope: Use 'exertion conditioner' in the four-bases-of-power formula.
translation_policy.when_not_to_apply: Do not import volitional-formation language from the aggregate sense of saṅkhāra, and do not merge padhāna with sammā-vāyāma.
translation_policy.drift_risk: Prevents the compound drifting out of the conditioner family and prevents exertion and effort collapsing into one word.
